#75910. Juiced unveils another lower-cost moto-styled electric bike: Scrambler Core

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1001 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Juiced unveils another lower-cost moto-styled electric bike: Scrambler Core

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a latest, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core.
  • The new Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.
  • Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a latest, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core. The new bike keeps much of the moto-inspired styling and performance of the existing Scrambler Hardtail, but trims back several components to knock several hundred dollars off the price.

The new Scrambler Core starts at $1,399, compared to $1,699 for the existing Scrambler Hardtail.

Juiced is also offering a $1,599 long-range version of the Core, as well as a smaller “Midsize” frame that should make the bike much more accessible to shorter riders – and, perhaps more importantly, teenagers.

Teens are a major part of the moto-style e-bike market, and Juiced has designed its Scrambler e-bikes as a safer option for those younger riders. In addition to ensuring street-legal performance for most major markets, Juiced rolled out a feature known as Speed Lock, which is essentially a parental control option that lets a parent or guardian set a lower speed limit using a PIN code that prevents their teen from later modifying the speed limit.

Recent findings suggest that the launch comes as part of the rebirth of Juiced Bikes following the brand’s acquisition last year. The manufacturer was founded in 2009 and was acquired in 2025 by the co-founders of Lectric Ebikes, who have since brought the brand back with a upcoming generation of its popular Scrambler platform.

The biggest changes appear to be in the powertrain, battery, brakes, and suspension.

The standard Scrambler Hardtail introduced earlier this year set the standard for the flagship models by using a 750W nominal motor with 90 Nm of torque and reaching 28 mph (45 km/h). Its 52V 19.2Ah battery provides nearly 1 kWh of capacity and a claimed range of up to 60 miles (96 km).

Industry observers note that the Scrambler Core steps down to a 500W nominal rear hub motor rated for 1,176W peak and 80 Nm of torque. Top speed is also reduced slightly to 25 mph (40 km/h), while the throttle is limited to 20 mph (32 km/h). Importantly, though, Juiced has retained its 52V architecture, meaning this is still a fairly punchy setup rather than a dramatically detuned budget bike.

Industry observers note that battery capacity takes a hit as well. The standard Core gets a 52V 10Ah battery with 520 Wh of capacity, rated for up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Spending another $200 gets the Core Long-Range with a 52V 15Ah, 780Wh battery and a claimed 60-mile (96 km) maximum range. As with nearly all e-bikes, expect real-world range to fall short of the idealized advertised numbers, which are generally only achievable under the lowest power pedal assist.

Juiced also traded the Talon P4 four-piston hydraulic brakes found on the more expensive Scrambler for Talon P2 two-piston brakes. The KKE inverted fork with 140mm of travel is gone too, replaced by a more conventional aluminum triple-crown fork with 100mm of travel.

According to recent reports, those are meaningful downgrades, but they’re also largely the kinds of changes I’d expect to see when trying to shave $300 off an already competitively priced moto-style e-bike. It’s a strategy we’ve seen play out before in the industry, helping lower costs for riders who want a flagship bike but don’t necessarily want to pay flagship prices.

It has been revealed that even so, notable features remain to help maintain the look and feel of the Juiced Scrambler line. The Core still gets 20 x 4-inch fat tires, hydraulic disc brakes, a frame-integrated TFT display, four pedal-assist levels, a headlight, taillight, brake light, and turn signals. It’s a single-speed setup and weighs 73 lb (33 kg), while being rated for a 300 lb (136 kg) payload.

Perhaps the more interesting addition is the Scrambler Core Midsize.

While the regular Core is recommended for riders 5’2” and taller, the Midsize drops that figure to just 4’10”. Pricing remains the same: $1,399 with the 520Wh battery or $1,599 with the 780Wh long-range pack.

Sources indicate that and with an eye towards safety, the Core and Core Mini retain Juiced’s PIN-protected parental speed lock. Parents can set the motor-assisted top speed anywhere from 1-25 mph and lock the setting behind a four-digit PIN. That makes even more sense on the Midsize version, which seems tailor-made for younger riders who want the moto-style look but may not yet comfortably fit the larger Scrambler.

Industry observers note that the Core is launching in several decidedly Juiced color names, including Black Nectar, Fruit Punch, Sour Grape, White Grape, Berry Freeze, and Blood Orange, though availability varies between frame sizes and battery configurations. Juiced indicates preorders are expected to begin shipping around the end of the month.

According to recent reports, at $1,399, the Scrambler Core feels like a logical extension of Juiced’s rebooted lineup. You lose some battery, motor power, braking hardware, suspension travel, and a few mph compared to the Hardtail, but the underlying recipe is largely intact. For riders who mostly want the Scrambler look and feel – or parents shopping for a smaller rider – saving $300 may be a pretty compelling trade. Especially when you consider that the original Juiced Scrambler already led the industry in value for moto-style e-bikes from reputable brands.

Toss in the strong backing from Lectric and the 3-year warranty, and it’s hard to consider much else among the competition.

At the time of writing, SHIB remains down 5.73% over the last 24 hours to $0.00000362. Just below SHIB's current price, a large buy wall has emerged, with Binance's spot order book revealing 17.92 trillion SHIB positioned at $0.00000361.

SHIB is exhibiting a strong accumulation of buy orders, which could signal a key support level as traders monitor buyers’ ability to soak up selling pressure.

A buy wall occurs when a lot of limit buy orders are stacked up around some price level and can show strong buying interest, providing temporary support if market participants are willing to fill those orders.

According to recent reports, now, if the price of Shiba Inu goes lower, then the 17.92 trillion SHIB order concentration that was reported could be an key area to watch. If the orders get filled and remain there, they could help absorb some of the selling pressure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting newly introduced safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

Recent findings suggest that the newly introduced feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.

I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

According to recent reports, that’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a big difference.

Of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

In a recent development, the feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin claims location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Big Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

This is cool but requires both a Garmin product and the Waze app. IMHO better to equip newly introduced cars and trucks with bicycle and pedestrian detection.

Garmin LiveTrack itself is free for customers with compatible Garmin devices and previously allowed cyclists to share their live location, speed, route, and other information with friends and family. I’ve used it myself as a safety feature when venturing off-road and on longer solo journeys. The Waze integration essentially expands that safety net to nearby motorists.

There’s obviously one substantial limitation: You need to be riding with a compatible Garmin device, and the driver needs to be using Waze.

But with Waze claiming around 200 million people globally and Garmin being one of the biggest names in cycling computers and fitness watches, that’s not exactly a tiny Venn diagram.

Anything that gives drivers another chance to see cyclists before actually seeing them sounds like a win to me.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the United Kingdom has moved beyond simply asking how crypto should be regulated in 2026.
  • The changes are being led by four key institutions: the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), HM Treasury (HMT), the Bank of England (BoE) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC).
  • Here’s a closer look at the UK’s crypto regulations in 2026, the latest changes and what they mean for businesses and investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the United Kingdom has moved beyond simply asking how crypto should be regulated in 2026. The main rules have now been written into law, firms are preparing for authorization, tax authorities are building reporting systems, and regulators are defining how stablecoins, exchanges, custody, staking and market activity will be supervised.

The changes are being led by four key institutions: the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), HM Treasury (HMT), the Bank of England (BoE) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC).

Here’s a closer look at the UK’s crypto regulations in 2026, the latest changes and what they mean for businesses and investors.

The UK’s Cryptoasset Reporting Framework (CARF) took effect on January 1, 2026. Under the framework, crypto exchanges, brokers, and other service providers must collect customer identity and transaction data. The first reports cover 2026 activity and are due by May 31, 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), through consultation paper CP26/4, proposed applying Consumer Duty, customer protection, safeguarding, training and reporting requirements to crypto firms. The consultation closed on March 12, and the FCA published the final rules on June 30.

On February 4, Parliament formally enacted the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026. Treasury commissioners Stephen Morgan and Christian Wakeford signed the legislation, which brings crypto trading, custody, stablecoins and staking under FCA regulation.

However, the regime is scheduled to take effect on October 25, 2027.

It has been revealed that HM Treasury published a draft proposal to move certain activities involving UK-issued stablecoins from general crypto trading rules to a separate payments framework. At the same time, the FCA opened a consultation to clarify which crypto activities fall under its supervision. The consultation closed on June 3, 2026.

Sources indicate that the FCA published PS26/9, covering cryptoasset admissions, public offers and market abuse. The rules introduce disclosure requirements, due diligence standards and controls against insider dealing and market manipulation on regulated crypto trading platforms.

Industry observers note that HMRC published draft legislation to change how crypto loans and liquidity pools are taxed. The proposal aims to prevent owners from facing Capital Gains Tax (CGT) on certain DeFi activities when they have not actually received cash or sold their assets. The government later confirmed the change in its October 28 Autumn Budget.

Industry observers note that HM Treasury laid the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations before Parliament. The amendments cover stablecoin payment arrangements, temporary settlement services, proprietary trading and technical services involving decentralised protocols.

Industry observers note that the FCA published PS26/18, explaining which crypto activities require regulatory approval under the fresh framework. Existing crypto businesses can apply for permission to operate under the new regime until February 28, 2027, to qualify for transitional protections.

Sources indicate that chancellor John Healey presented the UK Budget 2026, confirming plans to change the tax treatment of eligible stablecoins, cryptoasset loans and liquidity pools. The government included these measures in its plans for Finance Bill 2026–27.

HMRC updated its CARF reporting guidance, explaining how crypto businesses must submit customer and transaction information. It removed the planned January 2027 reporting start date because its online service was not ready. The first reporting deadline remains May 31, 2027.

In a recent development, treasury commissioners Christian Wakeford and Shaun Davies signed the Cryptoassets (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2026. The changes exempt certain market-making, proprietary trading, and technical services from specific authorisation requirements. Most provisions took effect the following day.

According to recent reports, the UK does not have one single crypto regulator. Instead, responsibilities are divided between four key regulators.Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

Industry observers note that the FCA is the main day-to-day regulator for crypto firms. Its responsibilities include anti-money laundering registration, financial promotion rules, market abuse requirements, and consumer protection.

In a recent development, the Bank of England focuses on financial stability and has a larger role in stablecoins. It will jointly supervise systemic stablecoins with the FCA and runs the Digital Securities Sandbox.

According to recent reports, HM Treasury is responsible for designing the UK’s broader legislative framework. It determines which crypto activities fall within the statutory regulatory perimeter and can designate a stablecoin or payment system as systemic under the Banking Act 2009.

Sources indicate that HMRC handles crypto taxes, including Capital Gains Tax, Income Tax and Corporation Tax. It also oversees the UK’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).

Sources indicate that crypto mining is legal in the UK and does not require an FCA licence. However, miners must follow HMRC tax rules and meet their electricity supply and business requirements.

HMRC taxes mining rewards based on whether the activity is a hobby or a business. Hobby miners generally pay Income Tax on their rewards, while commercial miners pay tax on trading profits and may deduct eligible business expenses.

It has been revealed that miners who later sell, swap or spend their coins may also pay Capital Gains Tax on any increase in value. For the 2026/27 tax year, the annual CGT allowance is £3,000, with rates of 18% and 24%.

Crypto remains a significant retail asset in the UK despite tighter regulation. Around 8% of UK adults owned crypto in 2026. That is down from 12% in 2024 but double the 4% recorded in 2021.

Overall crypto awareness remains high at 91%.

The UK government holds around 61,245 Bitcoin (BTC), making it the third-largest government Bitcoin holder after the US and China. These holdings are worth an estimated $3.5 billion to $3.8 billion.

The UK did not buy these Bitcoins for a national crypto reserve.

More than 61,000 BTC were seized by London’s Metropolitan Police during an investigation into Zhimin Qian, who ran a large investment fraud in China between 2014 and 2017 before fleeing to the UK.

The most important date ahead is October 25, 2027, when the full crypto regulatory regime is scheduled to take effect.

Before that deadline, existing firms have to navigate the FCA authorization process, with the key application deadline for transitional protections set for February 28, 2027.

HMRC will also begin receiving the first CARF reports covering 2026 activity by May 31, 2027.

That makes 2027 a turning point for the UK crypto industry.

The FCA regulates cryptoassets, working with HM Treasury and the Bank of England on comprehensive frameworks.

In a recent development, A buy wall occurs when a large volume of buy orders is concentrated around a particular price level on an exchange's order book. In a recent development, who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

Recent findings suggest that the Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the new i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse.

BMW stated the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The fresh i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW remarked the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s new i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the fresh i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW noted the upcoming 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

With an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

Very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

Like the fresh iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The newly introduced BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.

Why This Analyst Isn’t Rushing to Buy XRP Below $1 Despite Predicting an Explosive Rally to $10

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that XRP’s return below the psychologically important $1 level hasn’t convinced every investor that it is time to buy the dip.
  • In a November 19 post on X, crypto trader VirtualBacon identified the $1 price level as a potential bottoming zone for XRP in the current market cycle.
  • “For me, $1 is roughly the bottom area for this cycle,” he stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that XRP’s return below the psychologically important $1 level hasn’t convinced every investor that it is time to buy the dip. Despite believing the payments-based token could eventually climb to a staggering $10, one trader is holding back. His cautious stance raises an interesting question: if XRP has such massive upside potential, why is he waiting on the sidelines?

In a November 19 post on X, crypto trader VirtualBacon identified the $1 price level as a potential bottoming zone for XRP in the current market cycle. The analyst suggested that the cryptocurrency may be approaching the lower end of its correction, even as selling pressure continues to weigh on its price.

“For me, $1 is roughly the bottom area for this cycle,” he stated.

While he described the $1 mark as the approximate bottoming zone for XRP during the ongoing cycle, he did not suggest that a definitive price floor had already been established.

It has been revealed that his hesitation stems from the belief that investors will still have plenty of opportunities to accumulate alternative cryptocurrencies even after the broader market begins recovering. In his view, many altcoins could remain relatively cheap early in the next market rebound, meaning investors don’t necessarily need to rush into XRP before its downtrend runs its course.

“I’m not buying it yet,” he explained, making it clear that he would rather wait for a more favorable entry point than rush into the market.

XRP was trading at $0.9647 at the time of publication, down 2.3% over the previous 24 hours. The latest pullback followed a brief recovery to $1 on November 18, 2026, which proved short-lived as investors took profits, pushing the token back below the key psychological threshold.

Although VirtualBacon is not ready to accumulate XRP at current prices, he remains optimistic about its longer-term potential. The pundit believes the cryptocurrency could eventually reach $10, although he sees limited room for significant gains beyond that valuation.

In a recent development, A rally to $10 would represent a major milestone for XRP, pushing its market capitalization to approximately $635 billion based on a circulating supply of 63.52 billion tokens. This would place the cryptocurrency among the largest digital assets by market value and require its valuation to grow more than tenfold from current levels.

The projected price target also highlights the scale of growth XRP would need. At $10 per token, its fully diluted valuation, calculated using the maximum supply of 100 billion XRP, would reach approximately $1 trillion.

However, reaching such a valuation would require sustained demand, increased market participation, and significant capital flowing into the cryptocurrency. Notably, while VirtualBacon considers $10 achievable over the longer term, his outlook suggests that he sees this level as a more realistic upper target rather than expecting XRP to deliver substantially higher gains.

The Ethereum Foundation-linked wallet dumped another 2,500 $ETH ($3.88M), according to the Arkham database.

Recent findings suggest that wallet “0x5CBC” holds around $44.8 million in crypto, including $38.4 million of SUSDS and $6.41 million of Ethereum. Its latest transfer was on November 21, 2026.

Previously, another two wallets linked to the Ethereum Foundation transferred 4,393 ETH ($11.1 million at that time) to the Kraken exchange on October 12.

In a recent development, this transactions are not impulsive moves but part of a carefully planned 10-year strategy. Over the past decade, a total of 49,751 ETH has been sent from these addresses to exchanges.

It has been revealed that ethereum is presently going through one of its most challenging times in recent memory. Investor sentiment is still low, network activity has dispersed throughout Layer-2 solutions.

In addition to that, Ethereum has spent most of 2026 underperforming many rival ecosystems.

Industry observers note that earlier this year, Hsiao-Wei Wang has stepped down from the roles of co-executive director and board member of the Ethereum Foundation. In February, fellow co-Executive Director Tomasz Stańczak also stepped down.

Industry observers note that ethereum foundation has been selling ETH in 2026 during steep price movements, both up and down. For instance, BitMine acquired 10,000 ETH at an average price of $2,292 this June.

A similar sale one week earlier, where another 10,000 ETH was sold at $2,387 per coin.

On Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

Bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions.

Ethereum fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Industry News: The Healthiest Thing You Can Do for Your Prostate at Age 50

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (712 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, prostate cancer is the second leading cause of cancer deaths in men, so you’d think doctors would be adamant about screening guys for it.
  • Many guys didn’t know whether they should get it or not.
  • It has been revealed that the American Cancer Society just came out with fresh guidelines that for the first time, unequivocally say that men should get the screening test.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, prostate cancer is the second leading cause of cancer deaths in men, so you’d think doctors would be adamant about screening guys for it. Yet for years, prostate cancer screening via the PSA (prostate-specific antigen) test has been plagued by vague recommendations, and some back-and-forth messaging that flipped between “get it” and “the benefits might not be worth it.” Until recently, organizations including the American Cancer Society (ACS) used to give a recommendation that at age 50, guys should talk with their doctors about screening, then engage in a process of “shared decision-making” about whether to get the test.

Many guys didn’t know whether they should get it or not. Without a clear recommendation, it was easy for some to think this PSA blood test wasn’t very crucial to do at all. The landscape has changed.

It has been revealed that the American Cancer Society just came out with fresh guidelines that for the first time, unequivocally say that men should get the screening test. Guys at average risk should start at age 50. Guys at higher risk (more on that later) should start at 45.

Why that’s a big deal: “The latest guideline not only gets rid of shared decision-making, which is really difficult to execute, is subject to bias, and is really time-intensive,” says Yaw Nyame, MD, of the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center at the University of Washington Medical Center. “But it couples that with a better understanding of what present-day prostate cancer screening is.”.

According to recent reports, today, the PSA test is “just the first step, not the final answer,” says William Dahut, MD, chief scientific officer at ACS, and a contributing author to the guidelines. “It is a simple blood test, and an elevated result does not automatically mean cancer of the need for a biopsy.” Many more tools including MRIs and biomarkers help physicians drill down on who needs additional testing. “Our goal is to find prostate cancer earlier, while avoiding unnecessary procedures and treatment,” Dr. Dahut adds.

What changed that prompted the revised recommendations? “It’s notable to understand that guidance evolves as the evidence does,” says Dr. Dahut. Research has piled up to indicate that PSA screening reduces prostate cancer deaths.

Sources indicate that “We do not need to make a disclaimer that maybe you should, maybe you shouldn’t do it. Everyone should do it and you should start early, especially if you have a higher risk of cancer,” indicates Dr. Nyame, who was on the expert panel that reviewed the new ACS screening guidelines.

While all men should get the test, according to the latest guidelines, it’s not a “one size fits all” screening recommendation, Dr. Nyame explains. Recommendations vary according to risk. Find your category and screen according to that.

These are the fresh ACS guidelines for who and when:.

Other prostate screening guidelines came out earlier in 2026 from the American Urological Association (AUA) and the Society for Urologic Oncology (SUO) that had slightly different recommendations for the age at which you should start screening. What gives? The difference in recommended age and frequency of screening “has to do with how the guideline creators are viewing the different studies that they’re using to support their decision making,” Dr. Nyame says.

It doesn’t mean guys should throw up their hands and do nothing in frustration. “The AUA/SUO and ACS guidelines recognize the benefit of knowing a PSA test result earlier in life. A PSA test in the 40- to 50-year age range is a good predictor of the likelihood someone has or will develop a clinically significant prostate cancer,” says James A. Eastham, MD, chief of the urology service, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. A higher level early in life is a strong signal that you need to be really diligent about checking your PSA.

Sources indicate that “We’ve watched prostate cancer incidence increase—especially metastatic cancer, for over a decade now,” says Dr. Nyame. “And to know that we have a guideline that is so action-oriented toward reversing that course is really exciting.”.

Marty Munson, currently the health director of Men's Health, has been a health editor at properties including Marie Claire, Prevention, Shape and RealAge. She's also certified as a swim and triathlon coach.

Good Time to Buy Bitcoin? The Signals Worth Watching After the $55,122 Low

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Coinpedia

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that is the Bitcoin bottom in?
  • The Nasdaq fell more than 4% on November 20, and the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory.
  • Similarly, over the 30 days to November 18, Bitcoin fell 24.0%, Ether 26.5%, gold 10.2%, the Nasdaq 100 6.4% and the S&P 500 4.3%, according to Coinbase Institutional.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is the Bitcoin bottom in? Fresh November volatility has reopened the debate, putting historical on-chain thresholds and macro headwinds back in focus. Two questions run through this report, is Bitcoin cheap compared with what holders paid, and, is the selling finished? The data presented offers a clear framework.

The Nasdaq fell more than 4% on November 20, and the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory. Gold dropped to $3,513.54, a 14-month low.

Similarly, over the 30 days to November 18, Bitcoin fell 24.0%, Ether 26.5%, gold 10.2%, the Nasdaq 100 6.4% and the S&P 500 4.3%, according to Coinbase Institutional.

Sources indicate that bitcoin fell harder than stocks but alongside gold, which fits a move driven by liquidity and real yields rather than money shifting between assets. That makes a Bitcoin bottom harder to call from crypto signals alone.

In early November, 21Shares argued that Bitcoin’s cycle low came on June 30 at about $59,000, just over two years after the April 2024 halving and inside the window where earlier cycles bottomed.

Price has since traded below that level. Counted from the halving, June fits the pattern. Counted from the peak, the November low looks closer to normal.

Earlier bear markets lasted about a year from peak to low. This one took about nine months to reach June and has now run about 13.5. Three past cycles are a small sample, so the table frames the question without settling it.

The drawdown of about 55% is still the shallowest on record, against 77% to 86% before. Even the deeper scenario, $39,168 to $43,868, would be a drop of about 65% to 69% from the October 2025 high.

At $58,000, spot is about 1.09 times the realized price of $53,253 and about 1.19 times the LTH realized price of $48,563. A fall of about 8% would reach the realized price, and about 16% would reach the LTH level.

In a recent development, therefore, a further fall would put the typical holder underwater for the first time since early 2023. Spot is also about 23% below the early-November STH cost basis, so that band has already been broken. Each band matters for the Bitcoin bottom because earlier lows formed after price moved through them.

Industry observers note that holders are now split 46.82% in profit and 53.18% at a loss, measured against each coin’s realized cost basis. The same split has appeared at every major cycle bottom.

In 2011 price rose from $2.45 to $1,136 by 2013. Then, Bitcoin in 2015 it bottomed near $229 and reached $19,650 by 2017. Later, in 2018 it bottomed near $3,809 and rallied to $65,505 by 2021. As long-term trend continued, in 2022 it bottomed again near $16,966 and climbed to $126,411 by 2025.

Sources indicate that the profit and loss lines crossed in June 2026 and crossed again in November, in a similar price range. On that history, the next Bitcoin bottom is most likely to form in two likely zones either between $58,000 and $63,000 or $39,168–$43,868.

Sources indicate that the rallies have shrunk with each cycle: roughly 464 times from the 2011 low, 86 times from 2015, 17 times from 2018 and 7.5 times from 2022. Five cycles is a small sample, so the pattern shows where lows formed before and cannot promise where this one will.

In a recent development, in 2011, 2013, 2015, 2018 and 2022, lows formed after spot broke through the realized price and the short- and long-term holder bands. In 2026, only the short-term holder band has been broken. The realized price ($53,253) and LTH realized price ($48,563) are still intact, which favors a further fall of a couple of thousand dollars or more before a true Bitcoin bottom. The $39,168 to $43,868 area is where all the bands line up. This is a reading of past cycles, not a forecast.

It has been revealed that earlier bottoms formed when the realized profit/loss ratio reached 0.04 to 0.22. It reached 0.020 in November and has climbed back to 0.10. As a rough pychological projection suggests that, the bottoming process may be about 90% complete with about 10% left, though that cannot be measured and timed exactly yet. A reading of 0.10 sits at the middle of the range, so the market is in the zone but not necessarily at the floor, and earlier lows went as low as 0.04.

Tracked holders include 346 entities with 4,051,508 BTC, about 20.2% of the roughly 20.1 million coins in circulation.

In a recent development, US spot ETFs recorded $3.47 billion of net outflows from November 1 to 19, with 12 of 14 sessions negative. It is the worst month of the year for ETF flows, against $515.9 million out in October, and IBIT accounted for about 83% of the outflows through November 18. Net assets fell from $93.7 billion on November 9 to about $77.7 billion on November 18, while the funds still hold about 1.25 million BTC.

Moreover, Year-to-date flows turned negative at about −$2.5 billion after November 18 and passed −$3 billion after November 19, though IBIT is still up about $1.74 billion for the year through November 18.

Sources indicate that being below cost does not force a sale. Sales are forced by debt triggers, redemptions or lost funding. Strategy’s holdings are worth about $14.8 billion less than their cost at $58,000, and the MSCI decision does not require it to sell bitcoin. Twenty One reported $486.5 million of convertible notes secured by about 16,116 BTC in its Q3 letter. At $58,000 that collateral is worth about $935 million, a loan-to-value near 52%.

Blockworks data reported that 24 of the 25 largest crypto-treasury companies trade below the value of their holdings. Metaplanet’s mNAV was 0.49 on November 12, and it sold bitcoin last quarter to show it could draw on its holdings. Below 1x, issuing newly introduced shares dilutes holders, so the usual way to fund more bitcoin purchases is closed. Strategy’s mNAV was about 1.08x in mid-November, and one source had it below 1x on November 20. Its latest purchase was 485 BTC at $68,887, about $33 million, small next to $3.47 billion of ETF outflows.

On November 11, MSCI announced it will remove Strategy from the MSCI USA Index, and so from MSCI World and ACWI, at the close of November 30. Metaplanet leaves the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index the same day. Index funds tracking those benchmarks must sell the shares, and Strategy puts index-fund holdings at about 13 million shares. Whether that selling is absorbed without a fresh low will matter for the Bitcoin bottom.

The Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% on October 28 by a 10–2 vote, with both dissents favoring a hike. The minutes revealed near-unanimous support for more tightening, and a couple of participants floated a move bigger than 25 basis points.

In a recent development, CME FedWatch priced a 93.2% chance of a 25 bp hike on December 9 as of November 22, with 6.8% for no change and 0.0% for 50 bp. The 10-year yield slipped to 5.04% on November 20 from 5.04%, and the dollar stayed near a 19-month high.

Consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0, with one-year inflation expectations near 4%, and Brent crude is about 21% below its October peak. November CPI arrives December 10, a day after the decision.

The 10-year inflation-protected yield (DFII10) rose about 30 bp in November to roughly 2.88%–2.92%, its highest since 2008. That is the risk-free return after inflation, and Bitcoin has to compete with it.

According to recent reports, so far November fits the first case: Bitcoin fell alongside gold as real yields rose and ETFs sold. No decoupling has appeared yet, and a lasting Bitcoin bottom would be easier to trust if it did.

In a recent development, the Fear & Greed Index fell to 9 on November 20, its lowest since February. Other trackers read 10 to 12 on November 21, and the 2026 range runs from about 5 in February to about 78 in late September. So, current positioning is mixed.

It has been revealed that moreover, Funding is slightly negative at −0.0034%, yet 77.6% of accounts are long, a long/short ratio of 3.47. CoinGlass shows $1.30 billion of BTC liquidations over 24 hours, with longs making up $1.02 billion (78.82%) and shorts $274.6 million (21.18%).

Three moving averages sit near $75,500 above price, and a death cross is close. Extreme fear is a poor timing tool. Sentiment lows and price lows do not always coincide, and fear can last while price keeps falling, so sentiment alone cannot confirm a Bitcoin bottom.

The reading is mixed. Valuation, sentiment and the profit/loss ratio say a Bitcoin bottom is probably close in time. Price, flows and macro have not confirmed it, and the on-chain bands leave room for a lower low. The next markers are the realized price near $53,253, the LTH realized price near $48,563, a reclaim of $58,400–$59,650 and then $62,000–$66,000, the MSCI date on November 30, and the Fed decision on December 8–9.

These two major-cap altcoin peers are hitting close to historically-undervalued territory: a highly-awaited bottom sign?

French analyst EGRAG compared the 4-hour charts of XRP, Ethereum, Hedera, Bitcoin, Solana, and Stellar to assess which assets are showing relative strength after recent lows.

The mainstream French crypto chart analyst’s review centers on price reaction, volume-profile location, and the distance remaining to each coin’s Value Area Low (VAL).

In a recent development, XRP is holding above its recent low without returning for a full retest. Solana is behaving in a similar fashion, maintaining its recovery structure. Stellar (XLM) is tracking XRP but appears slightly weaker. Ethereum (ETH) is retesting its lows, with a potential higher low developing.

Bitcoin (BTC) also retested and printed a slightly higher high. Hedera’s HBAR was retested with a lower high, the most shaky local structure among the six.

Distance to reclaim the VAL currently ranks as follows:.

Sources indicate that XRP and Stellar (XLM) are the nearest to re-entering their value areas. Bitcoin demonstrates the more constructive local recovery structure among the larger-cap assets, even though it remains farther from its VAL than the two payment-focused names.

A double bottom is not confirmed simply because price holds above a prior low. The analysis treats bottoming as a process rather than a single candle. Early strength is marked by reclaiming the VAL.

Industry observers note that #CRYPTO – 6 COINS, WHO IS SHOWING STRENGTH? #XRP – #ETH – #HBAR – #BTC – #SOL – #XLM FOLLOW THE PRICE, VOLUME & STRUCTURE! 👀The 4H charts reveal different reactions after the recent lows:▫️ #XRP: Holding above its recent low without a full retest.▫️ #ETH: Retesting the… pic.twitter.com/IFPBMuh7NJ.

Structural confirmation requires a break of the local high. Stronger bullish conviction needs a reclaim of the Point of Control (POC) accompanied by volume.

Sources indicate that the 4-hour volume profiles show each asset still trading below or near the lower boundary of its recent value area. Acceptance back inside the value area, followed by a move toward the POC, would shift the local bias.

Until that occurs, the charts remain in a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed reversal.

As of November 19, 2026, approximate prices stood near 63,700–64,000 for Bitcoin, $1,810 for Ethereum, $0.99 for XRP, $75 for Solana (SOL), $0.138 for Stellar (XLM) & $0.056 for Hedera Hashgraph (HBAR).

The broader market remains under moderate pressure, with Bitcoin dominance elevated and the Fear & Greed Index in Extreme Fear territory for consecutive days now.

Industry observers note that the XRP coin & Stellar Lumens (XLM) are the nearest to early strength signals. Bitcoin’s slightly higher high on the retest is the more constructive structural note among the majors.

Industry observers note that confirmation across the group still requires a break of local highs and a return into the value area with volume. Until those conditions are met, the recovery remains unconfirmed.

Sources indicate that the daily chart of XRP has yielded a death cross, the first time the signal has popped up in 2026. XRP experienced a death cross on its daily chart in November 2025 and then entered a downtrend for several months before a recovery in August 2026.

Industry observers note that buoyed by optimism around favorable crypto regulation, XRP had already seen a golden cross in September 2026 before this. But that didn’t last long. The Senate stalled on the Clarity Act, a bill on crypto market structure.

Since then, the wider crypto market has struggled. The declines deepened in late October, as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and spending fueled a broad tech sell-off. They were compounded by the $6.3 billion Binance hack and weakening institutional ETF demand.

Throughout November, the crypto market has struggled due to a combination of dollar strength and leveraged liquidations.

The 50 DMA fell below the 200 DMA on the daily chart, completing a death cross pattern, coinciding with a sharp decline that took XRP below a key support and left leveraged traders nursing heavy losses.

As seen on the monthly chart, XRP has declined below the monthly 50 MA, a key level that supported its 500% rise in November 2024.

It has been revealed that however, all hope is not lost as the token’s daily relative strength index has dropped below 30, a level generally considered oversold. That can accompany a short-term rebound, but it does not fully establish that the decline has ended.

In a recent discussion on CNBC, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse expressed hope for a crypto rebound.

The Shiba Inu exchange activity has remained bearish as the broader crypto market continues to face persistent selling pressure, causing major assets to retest multi-year lows.

While other leading cryptocurrencies are still facing intense sell-offs from traders, the Shiba Inu ecosystem is beginning to signal a shift in market trend.

Although momentum still remains down and Shiba Inu exchange activity has stayed bearish, the latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that the intense selling pressure seen in the past day is finally easing.

The data shows that the Shiba Inu exchange netflow has faded to just about 18 billion SHIB on November 21, a substantial decrease from the nearly half a trillion SHIB recorded the previous day.

It is important to note that the current SHIB netflow still reflects a positive balance, which indicates sustained dominance by bear traders.

However, the slowdown to about 18 billion SHIB reveals that SHIB selling has decreased significantly even though sellers are not yet fully wiped out, providing a relief signal amid the growing market fear.

Although the current positive balance in the SHIB netflow shows that the number of SHIB tokens moved to exchanges for sell-off attempts is about 18 billion higher than the number purchased, its price movement is already turning bullish.

Latest market data reveals that Shiba Inu has surged by 1.51% over the last 24 hours, bringing its price to $0.000003625 as of the time of writing.

This suggests that demand is gradually returning to the SHIB ecosystem after multiple weeks of prolonged volatility. However, it remains uncertain whether the sudden price reversal is just a brief relief rally or a major recovery.

#75885. James Gray on Paper Tiger, Adam Driver, and Why Great Leading Men Need Danger and Vulnerability

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2852 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

James Gray on Paper Tiger, Adam Driver, and Why Great Leading Men Need Danger and Vulnerability

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • ONCE YOU’VE GONE to outer space with Brad Pitt and almost gotten eaten in the Amazon, where else is there to head but home?
  • That resulted, first, in 2022’s Armageddon Time, a largely autobiographical story of a young Gray growing up in Queens with his imperfect parents (Anne Hathaway and Jeremy Strong) and loving grandfather (Anthony Hopkins).
  • Sources indicate that the new film once again features characters explicitly based on his parents, this time with the bespectacled father, Irwin, played by Miles Teller and the expressive mother, Hester, played by Scarlett Johansson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ONCE YOU’VE GONE to outer space with Brad Pitt and almost gotten eaten in the Amazon, where else is there to head but home? That’s the question filmmaker James Gray asked himself after wrapping the World War I-era adventure epic The Lost City of Z and the celestial adventure Ad Astra. His answer: “I guess the conscious desire was to go back to what I know.”.

That resulted, first, in 2022’s Armageddon Time, a largely autobiographical story of a young Gray growing up in Queens with his imperfect parents (Anne Hathaway and Jeremy Strong) and loving grandfather (Anthony Hopkins). His latest film, Paper Tiger, was originally conceived as a sequel to that one, but eventually settled into a separate mostly autobiographical and intimate tale of the director’s youth.

Sources indicate that the new film once again features characters explicitly based on his parents, this time with the bespectacled father, Irwin, played by Miles Teller and the expressive mother, Hester, played by Scarlett Johansson. Naive Irwin gets drawn into a sketchy business initiative by his brash brother Gary, a former cop and ambitious entrepreneur played by Adam Driver—and things only go south when Irwin proudly decides to show his new venture off to his sons and sees something he should not have.

Paper Tiger also marks a return to Gray’s roots as a teller of crime stories that will stop you in your tracks. (Longtime fans will remember he made his directorial debut with the Tim Roth-led hitman thriller Little Odessa in 1994.) But what could be just another crime drama in the hands of a lesser filmmaker becomes a grounded human story about the downside of ambition with Gray. His films are arresting because they feel like they could happen to you, too.

It has been revealed that this new film, then, allowed the 57-year-old director to continue doing what he’s done his whole career: tell stories that, while lightly fictionalized, are still, at their core, true—regardless of genre. “I don’t see the movies as ‘crime dramas,’ even though clearly that’s what they are, because that’s part of the fabric of my young life growing up,” he indicates. “In my father’s case, and in my family’s case, it’s in our DNA. And so, for me, what is simply a memory of some sort, becomes quantifiable as a crime drama. Really, what you’re seeing is me trying to be very sincere with you about my own experience.”.

According to recent reports, it’s a story that’s been deep within him for a long time—and one he’s glad to have finally purged. “Now that I’ve gotten out of my system a little, I’m ready to expand the palette again,” he claims.

As Paper Tiger expands to a nationwide release in theaters, Gray spoke with Men’s Health about finding great leading men, mining his life for stories, and the key to making everything personal.

Plus—read Gray’s take on his former Lost City of Z star Robert Pattinson as James Bond, from just a couple of days before the casting became official.

MEN’S HEALTH: You’ve worked with stars like Brad Pitt, Joaquin Phoenix, and Charlie Hunnam, and now Paper Tiger adds Adam Driver and Miles Teller to that list. So, what makes a great leading man?

Sources indicate that JAMES GRAY: To be completely candid, some aspect of what you’re asking is unknowable until you see it on screen. It’s funny, I was reading about the casting of Peter O’Toole in Lawrence of Arabia. He had never done anything on screen, and all of a sudden they put him in the movie, and there’s magic. There are other people who you try to put in movies over and over again, and it never really clicks, for whatever reason. There’s an intangible quality to a great actor that we almost never can put our finger on.

Recent findings suggest that that said, I’m looking for an ability to convey two things at once: danger and vulnerability. A sensitivity. Often, what you find is it comes from intelligence. I’ve never worked with a great dumb actor. It does not exist. If the actor is marvelous—and I’ve been lucky enough to work with almost exclusively great actors—they are all brilliant in an emotional way. Does it mean they can quote Proust? No, but that doesn’t matter. They have an emotional awareness, and they can read a room, and they have a shrewdness. All of this stuff goes into the work, because if you have a close-up of an actor, you can immediately see what they’re thinking, if they are thinking. I’m looking for both danger and vulnerability, in kind of equal measure. And you see it over and over in great performances. In fact, I can only think of one performance in all of cinema history, really only one, that is both great and has no danger in it, and that would be what Jeff Bridges does in The Massive Lebowski. It has no danger at all, but it’s still a great performance. I’m not exactly sure how he pulled it off—it’s a real achievement. Maybe because he’s so sensitive and lovable in it that you fall for him, you know? But almost always, you have to have that aspect.

MH: When you’re casting for movies like Paper Tiger and Armageddon Time, which are ostensibly based on your own life, do you feel more of a pressure to make sure you get it right, as opposed to a story you’re perhaps a layer removed from, like The Lost City of Z?

Industry observers note that JG: It’s funny, I’m not sure how much difference there is. I know Lost City of Z is about a guy in Edwardian England going into Amazonia, but when I was conceiving of that movie, I never tried to distance myself from Percy Fawcett at all. I tried to, in fact, invest myself in him. He was a dreamer, someone who felt slighted by the system, and he wanted to prove himself over and over again. He didn’t have medals. He wanted to be celebrated, and he finally gets celebrated, and he needs more. All of that is in us.

So, your question is a very good one, but in all truth, I’m trying—and maybe you don’t succeed, of course—in all cases to put myself into the work. That’s what I would say is making something personal. That’s very different from making something autobiographical. Autobiographical adheres to the facts of your life, and it is true—these last two pictures have been quite autobiographical. But that’s just so that hopefully I have an easier time in getting at what it is that I’m thinking about. They’re different modes, but you’re still trying to do the same thing, which is to get at your interiority.

According to recent reports, MH: Miles Teller plays a character based on your father. I’ve never seen him do anything like what he does in Paper Tiger. What sold you on him?

Sources indicate that JG: I had seen a bunch of his work, and I’d also spoken to my esteemed assistant director, a wonderful, beautiful man named Doug Torres, who’d worked on a movie with Miles Teller. I knew about him through him, and also the people that had worked with him. I had seen a film called Bleed for This, where he plays Vinny Pazienza, and his performance has what we were just talking about. He’s a boxer, he has a toughness, but it’s a very vulnerable performance. I didn’t want to lean into the nebbish, schlub aspect to the character at all. I wanted the character to have a certain fortitude, because then the vulnerability can really come through. In other words, if you’re just casting a movie and the guy is a nerd or whatever, and you’re watching a nerd be nerdy, it’s not that interesting. What I found was that Miles has an alpha quality, but to see a tenderness inside of that was the thing that really interested me. And I saw it in that film.

Recent findings suggest that MH: Adam Driver is a sensational actor too. What was the appeal and experience of working with Adam?

In a recent development, JG: Adam has a very powerful onscreen dark quality, but he’s also open. He does completely different things from take to take. He’s always trying to find something newly introduced, something inventive. And he has tremendous craft. You can tell he’s really studied, and so you have both the craft and also he’s not in a rut. It’s just small things sometimes that you fall in love with. You’ve seen the film—he comes into the house, he brings Peter Luger’s, and he grabs the lamp, you know? A piece of set dressing. And he holds it under his face, and he notes, “Tonight, Luger’s is coming to us.” So, all of a sudden, he’s like a showman. It’s these little touches, where he understands character. And again, I know I’m repeating myself—this comes from intelligence. He’s incredibly intelligent. He sees bullshit a mile away. That is a very good thing for an actor. He is a truth-teller. Great actors are truth machines. They will not let you lie in a scene. They are always open to the moment.

MH: That character is fascinating to me, because in other movies like this, he might turn into a villain. But your story plays with such shades of gray, and it really stands out.

JG: The idea was to set up a scenario where you see the guy and your immediate impression might be “Oh, he’s a cop, he’s bringing food over. He must be a jerk, or he’s trying to scheme, or something.” But in fact it turns out the exact opposite; he had nothing but very pure intentions, and winds up sacrificing himself. That was very much part of taking the audience’s expectations and subverting them. Now, when you do something like that, you’re going to have, hopefully, a small percentage of the audience, whining and complaining, telling you What are you doing there? How could he be naive? But you’re also going to have a large percentage of the audience that’s going to embrace the fact that it’s not a cliché. I was leaning into the sense Adam has as an actor, saying, “Yes, but we’re going to trick you.” And in the end, he’s going to have a generosity and a nobility to his character.

MH: Adam’s character is really brash and confident—it seems like he’s used to getting what he wants and isn’t afraid to kick some ass. Miles’s character, on the other hand, is a lot more reserved and sometimes naive. How did you go about designing the story around these two guys who each carry a very different brand of masculinity and see the world in different ways?

Recent findings suggest that JG: It’s interesting you bring that up, because the operating principle of the movie… I was up very late one night, and I was watching—as one would—C-SPAN, I guess to try to put myself to sleep. And sometimes they televise the speeches that CEOs give at Davos, or that kind of thing. And I saw the CEO of a large corporation, and he was giving a speech, and he mentioned “95% of people don’t know there’s a game.” He said, “Of the remaining 5%, 4% know there’s a game and don’t know how to play it, and then the top 1% know how to play it, and will win.”.

I think his percentages are off—I think there are a lot more people who know there’s a game but don’t know how to play it, and that’s why we have a lot of anger in the world. But I thought of the story this way. You have Gary, a character who knows there’s a game, and knows how to play it, but he won’t make the ethical and moral compromises to win. You’ve got Irwin, who knows there’s a game, but has no idea how to play it. He’s smart—he’s an engineer. But he’s not shrewd. It’s a very different intelligence. And then you’ve got Scarlett, who probably knows there’s a game and maybe even knows how to play it, but fate has a different initiative for her. So, the movie was organized along these principles. That this idea that our society always rewards the smartest and best, that it’s a meritocracy, is not really true. It rewards a certain kind of smarts, along with a certain kind of willingness to compromise. I saw Adam and Miles in this framework.

MH: Do you often find the germ of an idea in mundane places like watching C-SPAN in the middle of the night?

JG: One of the horrible things about creativity, and it’s also one of the truths, is that it is a very mercurial, impatient, sometimes too patient, thing, and sometimes ideas come to you in the most random of ways. The biggest obligation you have to your imagination is your willingness to make the random idea connect. In other words, the essence of creativity is your ability to make connections. So, sometimes, you get inspiration from totally bizarre sources that you’d never imagine. It’s up to your imagination to be open to the randomness of these connections, and to try and pull from them the source of your idea. It can sometimes be totally different, like, you’re in nature, you get an idea, or you hear someone, a homeless man, say something—that’s an idea. It can come from anywhere. And then we have the idea, of course, of myth, to give it some kind of structure. But the random idea is of tremendous value. It can come from C-SPAN, or it can come from a baby crying. It’s all part of the soup.

MH: With this movie, as you have so often throughout your career, you’re mining from your own life. I’m sure many of these memories are painful, so how do you protect yourself emotionally and mentally to avoid falling into a dark and difficult place?

JG: It’s an excellent question, and the answer is that you kind of can’t. I wish I could give you a glib response—the way that I protect myself is X—but what I owe you, really, is something that is honest, that is sincere. And I don’t owe you the idea that I should make myself look good, and that you should like me. I owe you my own version of the truth. So, if I’m working, it’s not fun all the time. Sometimes, you have to do things that are uncomfortable, that are unflinching, that are honest. And it’s not always pleasant. We recreated a fight between my parents, when my mother hit my father. Scarlett and Miles created it almost exactly as I recall it. This is my job. That’s why I do it. I do it to give it to you. And through that, you find the air of compassion and sympathy for a collective experience.

According to recent reports, in other words, you’re not presenting a fantasy that has no relationship to honest emotion. And, by the way, when I say ‘fantasy,’ I don’t mean Star Wars can’t do it. Star Wars can do that. When he says, “No, Luke, I am your father,” that is actually connecting to something real, in the guise of a fantasy. When I say ‘fantasy,’ what I really mean is the filmmaker is trying to get you to like him or her or them, and that’s not my job. Sometimes you go to these unpleasant places, and it’s my job to cope.

MH: You’ve mentioned expanding your palette now that you’ve gotten these stories out of your system—do you have anything specific in mind? Is there anything you haven’t done yet that you want to try to tackle?

JG: I would love to do a Western. I would love to do a horror movie. I can’t believe I’m going to say this—I would love to do a musical. I don’t know what kind of shape the musical would take, but all of these genres are different forms of expression of the same ideas. I find the Westerns of John Ford unbelievably powerful to this day, because they’re always expressing something that’s inside Ford. Especially the films he made after World War II, which have such a thread of loss in them. And they’re very powerful to this day. You see John Wayne struggling with moral and ethical catastrophes in The Searchers, and you see a kind of post-war reckoning with what was a catastrophe of moral proportions in World War II, and you see it in John Wayne. You see the person of Ford coming out in that way, and using it in that canvas, the American West. That’s beautiful, and a way into the dark side of our personalities. Really, it becomes about me trying to find a story that will accommodate that, and that’s the difficult thing.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300.

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

According to recent reports, this drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

According to recent reports, on Thursday, November 19, AI company Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

Sources indicate that with the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

Sources indicate that coinGlass data shows $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

Recent findings suggest that according to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is at the moment trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

Bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

Similarly, minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released on the 18th of November, highlighted that nearly all officials expect further rate hikes. Notably, Governor Christopher Waller even floated a half-point move for December.

With the Fed target at 3.75%–4.00%, digital assets will not have an easy battle.

Ever since investors have moved away from crypto and into AI, the former’s fall has been nearly constant. For the uninitiated, on the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, thus valuing the AI manufacturer at roughly $1.5 trillion.

The news drew massive investor attention, pulling capital away from crypto markets as a result.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

According to recent reports, the crypto bloodbath will likely continue unless ETF flows stabilize or the Fed signals a pause. With the December 9 FOMC meeting as the only upcoming checkpoint, 60,000 is the next level for traders to watch. Losing it can tip Bitcoin deeper into the mid-50,000s.

  • Sources indicate that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal.
  • “One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that BYD and Geely have both approached the FIA about entering Formula 1, the sport’s governing body confirmed. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem named the two Chinese automakers while speaking at the Upcoming Economy Forum in Madrid, as first reported by Grande Prêmio.

Sources indicate that but there’s no open process for a 12th team, and neither company has a deal. The FIA is also pushing F1 toward the kind of engine an EV maker has the least reason to build.

“One of them was BYD and another was Geely,” Ben Sulayem mentioned of the manufacturers that have reached out about joining the grid.

He noted he suggested that BYD buy an existing team instead of starting a new one. BYD wasn’t interested in that route. It wants its own team, so Ben Sulayem told the company to come back with a “serious proposal” that reveals the project can work.

It has been revealed that he also made it clear that Chinese manufacturers won’t get special treatment. Any bid would go through the same process as other prospective entrants, and the rules won’t be rewritten to suit them. Right now, there’s no expansion process at all: the FIA isn’t actively looking for a 12th team.

Still, Ben Sulayem repeated that he’d like F1’s next newcomer to come from China, pointing to the country’s EV technology and the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai.

In a recent development, this isn’t new for BYD. Back in March, we reported that BYD was exploring a Formula 1 entry, either by buying a team or building one from scratch.

Sources indicate that in April, executive vice president Stella Li mentioned BYD had met F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in Shanghai and that an entry was “something we’re discussing.” By July, the tone had cooled. Li said “the dream is always there, but we don’t have a concrete agenda,” and special advisor Alfredo Altavilla set a clear condition: “We will never participate in Formula 1 just to put a sticker on the side of a car.”.

Altavilla remarked BYD would only consider F1 to the extent its technology can serve the sport.

Recent findings suggest that geely is the newly introduced name here. The group sold 3.02 million vehicles last year and owns Volvo, Polestar, and Lotus, a brand with decades of F1 history. It’s also heading into Canada next year as Chinese automakers push hard into new markets.

The last newcomer, Cadillac, took a long road. The FIA opened an expression-of-interest process in 2023, and GM’s team only joined the grid as the 11th team this season, running Ferrari power until its own power unit arrives. Audi got in the other way, by taking over Sauber.

It has been revealed that here’s where it gets awkward for an EV maker. The 2026 F1 power units split output roughly 50/50 between the combustion engine and electric power, with the MGU-K jumping to 350 kW.

According to recent reports, the FIA is already walking that back. In June, it agreed to shift the split to 60-40 in favor of combustion for 2027 and 2028. And Ben Sulayem has been pushing for V8 engines running on sustainable fuel with “minor electrification” for the next rules cycle, starting in 2031 at the latest, possibly 2030. Domenicali indicates F1 should have a package ready to discuss by the end of this year.

So the FIA president wants a Chinese EV maker on the grid, while pushing a rulebook that makes their main strength less relevant.

Recent findings suggest that we like the idea of BYD or Geely in F1. Chinese automakers have the money and the engineers, and they badly need brand prestige outside China. BYD in particular has been on a performance push with Yangwang, and F1 would be the loudest possible way to tell Europe it’s not just a cheap car brand.

they look for visibility/recognition on the world stage, regardless EVs. And in some (primitive) markets they market themselves as hybrids automakers, not as EV automakers.

They will make a hybrid power unit (which they already make anyway) to comply with the backward F1 regulations.

It has been revealed that but Ben Sulayem’s comments don’t move things much. There’s no entry process, BYD has already turned down his main suggestion, and Geely’s interest is a name dropped at a conference, not a bid.

A Chinese would likely be good for F1 as well. Motorsports are on the rise in China, and that would be the cherry on top in helping popularize the sport in the world’s largest market.

The bigger problem is the engine. Altavilla was clear that BYD isn’t interested in slapping a logo on a car. It wants F1 to showcase its technology, and BYD’s technology is batteries and electric drive. The FIA’s V8 push goes the other way. It’s hard to sell an EV giant on a sport that’s reducing the electric part of the powertrain.

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, has recorded a multi-month high in daily trading volume as the cryptocurrency market remains in the grip of extreme volatility.

The massive spike in trading volume comes after Bitcoin tanked to two-year lows on Nov. 21 before bouncing back sharply to regain ground toward the psychologically crucial $60,000 level.

The massive spike in trading volume comes in the wake of one of the biggest sell-offs in BTC this year.

In a recent development, on Nov. 21, the world’s largest cryptocurrency dropped as low as around $55,100, a level last seen in September 2024. The sharp decline in Bitcoin prices came as risk assets tumbled amid rising concerns over the U.S. stock market and the artificial intelligence (AI) sector, which weighed on investor sentiment.

Following the sharp plunge, Bitcoin managed to make a stunning comeback as the flagship cryptocurrency recovered to trade back above $60,000 and briefly pushed toward the $61,000 mark.

The comeback, however, was short-lived as BTC lost ground again and tanked below the crucial $60,000 mark.

BTC is presently trading at around $58,879, rising 5.4% in the last 24 hours, as per the latest data from CoinGecko.

Furthermore, the world’s largest cryptocurrency has a 24-hour trading volume of around $43.8 billion and has regained a market cap of $1.18 trillion.

According to recent reports, as per data from analytics firm CoinGlass, Bitcoin (BTC) futures trading volume stands at around $76.17 billion. On the other hand, the cryptocurrency's spot trading volume stands at $7.91 billion over the past 24 hours.

Despite the latest recovery, it is still trading 9.74% lower over the past seven days and more than 27% lower over the past month.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency is also down around 53.3% from its all-time high of $126,198.

Another massive wave of liquidations has swept through the cryptocurrency market following the latest recovery.

As per the latest data from CoinGlass, 85,533 traders have been liquidated in the last 24 hours, with total liquidations amounting to $562.12 million.

It is worth noting that around $406.13 million in liquidations were on the short side, while only $156 million were on the long side.

With regard to BTC, it alone accounts for around $346.18 million in liquidations, and a staggering 76.7% of those liquidations were on the bearish side.

At the moment, Bitcoin is unable to reclaim the $60,000 level with conviction.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased.
  • According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.
  • The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period. Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being said, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

Sources indicate that wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Sources indicate that institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That mentioned, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

This comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.
